data.head: # escher 0.4.0 — vision

body:
*Source: `escher-0.4.0-incubator/intent-0.4.0.md` (the overseer's assembly of the founder's words, 2026-10-29,
2026-11-04, 2026-11-18/19).*

data.head: ## The problem it advances

body:
escher is an agent-first UI framework: a UI an agent can see, drive and verify headless, and learn from the tool
alone. 0.3.0 closed with 17 of 17 capabilities verified and a cold-agent run of 0 wrong in 76 calls. Two things stand
in the way of the next step, 0.5.0's demo project. First, debts from 0.1.0–0.3.0 remain open. Second, escher's
world stops at the web-like box: an agent sees a canvas as one opaque element.

data.head: ## What 0.4.0 does

body:
- **Closes every debt of 0.1.0–0.3.0.** This covers the build directory's unbounded growth, upstream's new work, the
  README, and the open residuals. Each residual comes to the founder as a fork at its phase. One that waits on
  another project's release is stated as such.

- **A headless 2D canvas an agent sees inside.** The founder chose layers 1 and 3: an app paints a canvas from Rust
  and the canvas appears in a headless shot (layer 1). An agent reads the canvas as data, as draw commands and as
  virtual nodes that act like elements (layer 3). A `drag` verb and pan/zoom under a transform complete the surface.

- **The stand is the proof, modified for the canvas.** Circle Drawer moves onto a real canvas, and a new node-graph
  stand app is added.

data.head: ## Head of the version (fixed order)

body: The build directory's growth, then the upstream sync, then the README.

data.head: ## Out of this version

body: - The demo project and heavy modern HTML: 0.5.0.
- The wgpu canvas (layer 2) and the CPU renderer's custom-paint gap.
- A web Canvas 2D context for page scripts.
- The mutation tails, until the founder decides.
- Opt-in OTel export, the MCP revision `2026-07-28`, and the platform accessibility adapter's windowed witness.
- Viola's GUI on escher.
- New upstream PRs, which wait on #1083's reaction.

data.head: ## This version is done when

body:
Every capability below is verified headless on the stand or a fixture beside it. Every residual of 0.1.0–0.3.0 has
been fixed or kept by the founder's word with its reason. One cold-agent run on the stand has used the canvas as
data, a virtual node and `drag` at least once each, and it passes the 5 % wrong-call bar.

data.head: # escher 0.4.0 — intent

body:
escher is a fork of Blitz (DioxusLabs/blitz) turned into an AGENT-FIRST UI framework: a UI an agent can see, drive
and verify headless, and learn from the tool alone. 0.3.0 closed 2026-11-18 at `bc7661240`, 17 of 17 capabilities
verified; its cold-agent run read 0 wrong of 76 calls over seven stand apps for $1.03. 0.4.0 does two things: it
**closes every debt of 0.1.0–0.3.0**, and it takes escher past the web-like box with **a headless 2D canvas an
agent sees inside**. The demo project that shows everything escher can do is 0.5.0, not this version.

Assembled 2026-11-19 by the escher overseer from the founder's words of 2026-10-29, 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-18/19,
each verbatim in the overseer's `relays/intent-0.4.0-founder-2026-11-04.md` and
`relays/intent-0.4.0-founder-2026-11-18.md`. It replaces the preliminary `intent.md` beside it for this version;
that file's finding 1 (the tech demo), finding 2 (heavy modern HTML), §The demo's concept and its coverage table
are 0.5.0's material. Research beside this file: `canvas-research-2026-11-18.md`; history:
`canvas-and-node-graph.md`, `adapt-0.3.0-for-canvas.md`, `deferred-from-0.3.0.md`.

data.head: ## Principles for this version

body:
- **Two versions.** The founder, 2026-11-18: «Ну получается план примерно такой в 0.4.0 закрываем все долги с первых
  трех версий и делаем полную канвас хедлесс верификацию а потом в 0.5.0 строим демопроект который пказывает все
  что можно выжать из эшера и подтверждает каждую заявленную возможность».

- **The head of the version, in this order (the order is the overseer's reading, his to change):** the build
  directory's growth — «Да надо добавить в голову 0.4.0 разобраться с этим» (2026-11-19) — then the upstream sync
  and the README — «В голову 0.4.0 еще надо взять апстрим синк , обновление ридми для гита» (2026-11-19).

- **The canvas, layers 1 and 3.** The founder, 2026-10-29: «Ну я думаю для начала можно взять 1 3 это уже сильно
  расширит возможности, а 3д оставить на потом». Layer 1 is a 2D canvas painted headless; layer 3 is the agent
  seeing inside it through virtual nodes. The wgpu canvas (layer 2) is out.

- **The canvas is painted from Rust.** The founder, 2026-11-18: «Ну меня идея рисовать js внутри раст фреймворка в
  целом не особо прельщает, раст это скорость а эти маневры мне кажется только все замедлят». No web Canvas 2D
  context (`getContext('2d')`) for page scripts is built; an app paints through the scene API.

- **Observe the canvas as data, not pixels.** The founder, 2026-10-29: «Просто по идее если это параметрический 2д
  то мы можем обсервить это не только скриншотами». Screenshots stay for people and visual questions.

- **The stand is the proof, modified for the canvas.** The founder, 2026-11-19: «Проверять да будем стендом его надо
  будет модифицировать чтоб работу по канвасу можно было проверять», and of the overseer's two samples: «По поводу
  стендов да давай оба берем».

- **A cold-agent run on the stand closes the version, at the 5 % bar.** The founder: «Оставить 5 % (Recommended)»
  (2026-11-18), «Холодный прогон по стенду в конце берем» (2026-11-19).

data.head: ## Findings (OBSERVED → EXPECT)

body:
1. **The build directory grows without bound.**
   OBSERVED (2026-11-19 06:11Z, at `bc7661240`; the overseer's finding ES142): `target/debug/deps` held 773 GB,
   written at 83 to 162 GB a day since 2026-11-13. The weight is 193 integration-test binaries (185 files under
   `tests/blitz-tests/tests/`, 8 under `examples/seven_guis/tests/`) of about 145 MB each, each standing in 30 to
   65 stale hashes. During the night's mutation tier the host fell to 58 GB free of 930; a `cargo clean` removed
   896 GiB. The cause — a low-crate edit re-hashing every test binary while cargo collects nothing; feature sets
   differing between gate entries possibly multiplying it — is a hypothesis, not measured. The same audit reads
   duplication rising for two boundaries (3.80 → 3.81 → 3.89 %), all of it stand tests repeating each other's setup.
   EXPECT: the version's first entry measures the cause and mends it, and states the growth of a working day
   after the mend as a number. Levers seen, none chosen: one test binary per leg in place of one per file; a sweep
   of stale hashes at a wrap or a boundary; less debuginfo for test binaries.

2. **Upstream moved.**
   OBSERVED (2026-11-19 06:44Z, after a fetch): `upstream/main` at `5b8e7a268`, 209 commits not in the build
   branch, the ones earlier syncs left out on purpose among them (residual `res-7qgqygtj`: 102 at `e5305a4c1`, each
   with its reason — the git AnyRender pins, Dioxus 0.8 alpha, the CDP TCP listener `res-ipcah32k`). Upstream's
   status page lists `position: sticky` as in progress (blitz#887).
   EXPECT: an upstream-sync entry opens each epoch, as in 0.2.0 and 0.3.0: a real two-parent merge, our tests and
   CI proving our logic survived, each commit left out named with its reason.

3. **The README.**
   OBSERVED: `README.md:87` reads «### 0.3.0 — built, its cold-agent run passed» (the overseer's interim heading);
   0.1.0 and 0.2.0 read «done and verified». The version-end audit of 0.3.0 is recorded (ledger tx 2303).
   EXPECT: the README states 0.3.0 as closed, in the form the founder chooses at that entry's phase, and says what
   0.4.0 builds.

4. **Every debt of 0.1.0–0.3.0.**
   OBSERVED (the store's `open_residuals`, 22 rows at 2026-11-19; `deferred-from-0.3.0.md` mirrors fourteen of
   them; the founder's «Все 14» and «все долги с первых трех версий»):
   - the select list: its thumb not draggable (`res-ammkrycp`) · a highlighted row's contrast unread by the lint
     (`res-tym5wois`) · a larger authored font clipping (`res-2iu7qn2e`) · the highlight in no snapshot and no tree
     (`res-caouqg3t`) · a single select's `size` unread (`res-ysz67imk`);
   - the driver: `press` carries no Ctrl (`res-hfvjj77l`) · the UI graph not paged, 293,869 bytes on Cells, its
     form ruled `graph --part N` (`res-7cc5bi4k`) · handler coverage counting every ancestor listener a bubbling
     dispatch passed (`res-4dr3wt62`);
   - the engine: a focused control that no longer shows keeps focus and takes keys (`res-6k56erh6`) · a task
     polled during a Dioxus render acts on the previous render's document (`res-433ttjb2`) · a page script's
     `Math.random` unseeded (`res-jqbadec2`) · the error-boundary registry only grows (`res-k2zggoqx`);
   - dependencies and upstream: the RUSTSEC-2026-0459 ignore (`res-j4x7iiqc`) · upstream's test left out until
     Dioxus 0.8 (`res-xpkmxnvl`) · the left-out upstream delta (`res-7qgqygtj`) · the CDP listener's security
     amendment (`res-ipcah32k`) · the merge surfaces and standing notes (`res-xchmbfjr`, `res-vuvpa25q`,
     `res-q4s3p5ga`, `res-kk4tzmi5`, `res-derughab`);
   - CI: the WATCH on a macOS or iOS job cancelled with no runner (`res-q2tllspz`);
   - the code audit at the Epoch 6 boundary: `blitz-dom/src/document.rs` at 3,367 lines, 25 files over 800 lines,
     88 functions over the complexity ceiling; four surviving mutants at `apps/browser/src/capture.rs:86:5`.
   Outside this set and NOT decided (the founder, 2026-11-19: «по поводу мутантов я подумаю»): the mutation tails —
   escher-driver's 7 untested mutants, wpt's relative `TMPDIR`, blitz-dom whole. No entry is written for them.
   EXPECT: each residual gets a route entry, alone or grouped with its neighbours, and comes to the founder as a
   fork at its phase: fixed, or kept as a residual by his word with its reason. One that hangs on another's
   release (RUSTSEC, Dioxus 0.8) is stated as such, not forced. `drag` (finding 8) owns the select thumb.

5. **A 2D canvas painted headless.**
   OBSERVED (read 2026-11-18 on the tree after `bc7661240`, nothing built): an app paints through the `Widget`
   trait, `paint(&mut dyn RenderContext, styles, width, height, scale) -> Scene`
   (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/custom_widget.rs:75`), appended by `blitz-paint` behind the `custom-widget`
   feature (`render.rs:615`, `:1377`). Headless shots render through `VelloCpuImageRenderer`
   (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/screenshot.rs:83`), and the harness takes `blitz-paint` with
   `default-features = false` (`blitz-test-harness/Cargo.toml:18`), which drops `custom-widget` unless another
   crate unifies it: whether a headless shot paints a widget at all is unmeasured. The CPU backend paints
   `Paint::Custom` and `Paint::Resource` transparent with no warning. `<canvas src="N">` sets a
   `custom_paint_source_id` nothing reads. Upstream issue #1578: a widget's paint gets the border-box size and is
   placed at the content-box origin. No stand app holds a canvas; Circle Drawer's «canvas» is an ordinary element
   (`examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/circle_drawer.rs:83-88`).
   EXPECT: what an app paints into a canvas from Rust appears in a headless screenshot, measured on the stand
   first; canvas text draws from the bundled fonts (v030-14). Whether a canvas shot is byte-equal across CI's
   Linux, macOS and Windows hosts is measured, and required or given a stated tolerance by the founder's word.
   The stand's Circle Drawer moves onto a real canvas as the first sample.

6. **The canvas observed as data.**
   OBSERVED: anyrender records a scene as serde-serializable commands (Fill, Stroke, GlyphRun, PushLayer,
   PushClipLayer, PopLayer); `anyrender_serialize` 0.9.0 is in the workspace, used by `apps/browser` alone. No
   driver verb reads a canvas's content. Prior art (`canvas-research-2026-11-18.md` §3): Flutter's display-list
   test form — one line per op, layers as indentation; dumps generated from the types; heavy data by reference.
   EXPECT: a driver verb returns a canvas's draw commands as data — deterministic, independent of hardware,
   diffable between two states, grouped by virtual node where one covers the commands, with a summary level and a
   full level. Lint-like checks run inside a canvas (a label overflowing its region). What the verb may carry to
   a model provider is a boundary fork for the founder at its phase; the size of a dump is measured on the stand.

7. **Virtual nodes inside a canvas.**
   OBSERVED: a snapshot node needs an author id AND a DOM element (`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:153`),
   so an agent sees a canvas as one opaque element; the UI graph reserves no id form for a non-DOM node. Reserved
   already: `Placer::App { canvas }` in the `layout` verb (`packages/escher-driver/src/layout.rs:58`) and a
   commented `accessibility_tree` on `Widget` (`custom_widget.rs:144`). AccessKit carries nodes with no DOM
   behind them, with bounds and a transform on the parent.
   EXPECT: an app declares virtual nodes inside a canvas — an author key, a role, a name, a region. The driver
   treats them as elements: they appear in the snapshot and the diff, take `click`, carry refusal causes (covered,
   off-screen, disabled, and stale for a key that is gone), and reach the UI graph, «what can I do here», handler
   coverage, layout explained («placed by the app inside canvas X») and exploration. Regions give semantics and
   refusals; events still reach the widget as ordinary pointer events. The declaration's form — a list at each
   paint, or callbacks with invalidation — is a fork at its phase.

8. **A `drag` verb.**
   OBSERVED: the driver has fifteen verbs, none `drag` (`packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:709`;
   `command.rs:935,945` pin 15 and `(11, 3, 1)`). The harness holds `drag(from, to, steps)` and the mouse
   primitives (`packages/blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs:112-150`). Playwright and flutter_test both note that a
   drag in one jump silently fails in apps that listen to moves.
   EXPECT: `drag` moves from an element or a virtual node to another, or by an offset, through several
   interpolated moves by default; settled like every action, refused with a cause like every action, the source
   and the destination both checked first. The wire stays versioned; a recorded check carries the step and replay
   replays it; «what can I do here» lists `drag` where it applies. The select list's thumb is dragged by it.

9. **Pan and zoom under a transform.**
   OBSERVED: `visible_region` reads a clipping box where its transforms show it — «Exact under a translate and a
   scale; under a rotation it reads the bounding box» (`packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs:816`) — and was not
   proven on a pan/zoom container. The driver's `scroll` scrolls; nothing zooms. Speed with hundreds of positioned
   nodes is unmeasured.
   EXPECT: on the stand's pan/zoom surface, a target inside the transformed container is read, hit and acted on
   where it shows; a zoom by the wheel or a gesture is its own verb or a stated limit by the founder's word; the
   surface's speed is measured at a stated node count.

10. **The stand's canvas samples.**
    OBSERVED: the stand holds eight apps (counter, temperature converter, flight booker, timer, CRUD, circle
    drawer, cells, order), none with a canvas.
    EXPECT: two samples, built as the capabilities that need them land, each with its stand checks: Circle Drawer
    on a real canvas, its circles virtual nodes (findings 5–7); and a new stand app, a small node graph — three
    or four nodes with ports, wires as curves in a canvas, nodes dragged, a wire pulled port to port, the surface
    panned and zoomed (findings 8–9) — the groundwork for 0.5.0's demo.

11. **The cold-agent run.**
    OBSERVED: 0.2.0's run read 66 calls, 0 wrong, $0.82; 0.3.0's read 76 calls, 0 wrong, seven apps, $1.03, under
    the 5 % bar.
    EXPECT: 0.4.0 ends with one cold-agent run on the stand, the two canvas samples among its apps: the canvas
    read as data, a virtual node acted on and `drag` each used at least once, judged at 5 % wrong calls. The run's
    budget and its count are the founder's word at its phase.
